about: What a build of the consumer bundles reads when it runs with no network and no .git, and how to give it what it reads. Held by scripts/lib/offline_build.py (--check derives it from the crates graph, --build builds every bundle in a sandbox that has nothing else); the design is docs/target-build-contract.md section 5d.

source.tree: the files the repository tracks at the commit, without .git

submodules.commit: the gitlink the tree records at this path

commit_input.value: what `git describe --always --dirty=-modified --abbrev=40 --exclude=*` answers in a checkout of the commit: the commit of 40 lowercase hex digits for a clean tree
commit_input.without_it: the build names itself `release` where a checkout build names the commit

cargo.crates: every package of the lockfile, from crates.io, vendored (`cargo vendor --locked`); the lockfile has no git source

cc.what: a C compiler driver; rustc also calls it as the linker

ar.what: an archiver for the static libraries build scripts make

libclang.what: the libclang shared library and its resource headers, which bindgen loads while librocksdb-sys's build script runs

output_variables.note: variables a build script reads that change what it produces; a build identical to a checkout build leaves them unset

not_inputs.why: no build script of any bundle reads it: it is what wz's zenoh-c oracle lanes compare the drop-in against
